description: Executor.validate() reports every check (PROTOCOL_SPEC 12.8.1 principle 2, decision D-134) and reports module-level preflight/preview as 12.8.3 / 12.8.5.1 say (decision D-141). Before D-134 all three SDKs ran the dry run fail-fast: the first failing check ended it, and apcore-python and apcore-typescript also discarded every check that had passed before it. The one exception stays: after a failed `acl` check, module-level preflight() and preview() are withheld (12.8.5.1, pinned by preflight_disclosure.json). D-141: a module without preflight() MAY still yield a passed `module_preflight` check; preview() returning null adds no `module_preview` check; `predicted_changes` is always present, empty when nothing is predicted.

driver_contract.path: Drive the real Executor.validate() against a real Registry and a real ACL built from `input.acl_rules` / `input.default_effect`, with caller `input.caller_id` and inputs `input.inputs`.
driver_contract.module: Register the module of `module_contract` under `input.module_id` unless `input.module_id` names a module that is deliberately not registered (`register: false`). `input.implements_preflight` / `input.implements_preview` say whether the module defines those methods; `input.preview_returns_null` makes preview() return null instead of `preview_change`.
driver_contract.checks_present: Subset assertion: every named check appears in `checks`.
driver_contract.checks_absent: Every named check is absent from `checks` altogether.
driver_contract.failed_checks: Exact set of the checks whose `passed` is false.
driver_contract.passed_checks: Subset assertion: every named check appears with `passed: true`. This is what fails an implementation that drops the checks that passed before a failure.
driver_contract.optional_passed_checks: Each named check is either absent, or present with `passed: true` and no warnings (a MAY: D-141 allows it for a language that cannot tell a default method from an implemented one).
driver_contract.predicted_changes: `expected.predicted_changes_count` is the length of `predicted_changes`. `expected.predicted_changes_present: true` asserts the field is present as a list in the SDK's serialized result (Python dataclasses.asdict, TypeScript JSON.stringify, Rust serde_json::to_value), under `predicted_changes` (`predictedChanges` in TypeScript); absent or null fails.

test_cases.description: The control: a permitted caller with valid inputs.

D-134: the checks that passed before the failing one stay in the result. apcore-python and apcore-typescript returned only the failed `schema` check (plus `module_id`), dropping `module_lookup` and `acl`.

D-134: a failing check does not stop the checks after it. With the caller denied AND the inputs invalid, both failures are reported; every SDK stopped at `acl`. Module-level preflight/preview stay withheld after the ACL failure (12.8.5.1).

D-134's boundary: a check that needs the module is not recorded when there is no module. An implementation that reports a failed `schema` check for a module it never found fails here. The ACL permits every target, so `module_lookup` is the only check that can fail.
D-141: preview() returning null means no prediction is available, and records nothing. apcore-python and apcore-typescript added a passed `module_preview` check.
D-141: `predicted_changes` is always present. apcore-typescript left it undefined and apcore-rust skipped it when serializing an empty list.
D-141: a module that does not implement preflight() either records no `module_preflight` check or a passed one with no warnings; it never records a failed one.
